hypothesis: HT-Breakout entries whose completed five-minute breakout direction agrees with the completed-hour structural direction may outperform entries where those directions oppose after live costs.
decision: Continue rejecting a simple five-minute direction-agreement gate. The first resolved non-HYPE long, SOL, earned +$1.582877 after recorded fees and funding and moved all-live HT-Breakout performance from -$1.760917 to -$0.178040. Exact aligned outcomes improved to one win and four losses with -$0.028398 net, while opposed outcomes remain two wins and five losses with -$2.310562 net. This strengthens the separate hypothesis that side and market identity matter, but one SOL long cannot establish transferable edge. Keep the bidirectional v25 route unchanged and continue prospective side-separated measurement.
falsifier: Reconsider the direction-agreement rejection only if a predeclared prospective sample with complete causal coverage makes aligned outcomes materially positive and better than opposed outcomes after costs on an unopened venue window. Downgrade the long-side transfer hypothesis if additional BTC, ETH, or SOL longs lose after costs, or if repeated core-asset shorts recover to positive profit factor under the same execution and exit contract.
limitations: Only 12 of 19 live HT-Breakout closes have exact causal breakout-side relation coverage.
The SOL long is one lifecycle and cannot establish cross-asset transfer or durable side edge.
BTC and ETH still have no closed HT-Breakout long outcomes.
Historical profiles, position sizes, market regimes, and exit generations differ across the all-live record.
The 365-day replay uses modeled friction and cannot establish private live IOC fills or future performance.
Overlapping positions share portfolio capital and are not independent samples.
This journal revision grants no gating, ranking, sizing, routing, exit, or promotion authority.
